findings.title: Test bare class annotation upgrade
findings.why_it_matters: The added explicit-state transition for a bare endpoint followed only by :::class is an acceptance path, but the current class test also supplies a shape. That shape was already explicit, so the test would still pass if class annotations did not mark a bare placeholder explicit; a later shaped definition could then incorrectly replace it instead of producing the required duplicate warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parser case with `A --> E((End))`, then `A:::highlighted`, then a shaped `A[...]`; assert the first class-annotated declaration remains the process node, the later definition yields exactly one DUPLICATE_NODE warning at its location, and the class warning remains deterministic.
evidence: MermaidParser.withClassAnnotation now sets explicit: true, which is the only mechanism that upgrades a bare `A:::highlighted` endpoint.

The test at line 198 uses `A[Review order]:::highlighted`; parseEndpoint has already marked that shaped endpoint explicit before withClassAnnotation runs, so it cannot prove the new class-only state transition.
No added case puts a later explicit definition after a bare class-annotated declaration to verify first-explicit-wins behavior for that acceptance path.

testing_gaps: No test covers a bare edge-created placeholder upgraded solely by `:::class` and then followed by another explicit definition; this leaves the class-only first-explicit-wins branch unproven.
